newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saint-Louis eyes 4-5 bln Ffr cash holdings.
newsitem.headline: Saint-Louis eyes 4-5 bln Ffr cash holdings.

text.p: French sugar and paper group Saint-Louis plans to develop in the agro-food sector as it will have between four and five billion francs of cash in hand after the sale of its stake in prepared-meal unit Panzalim, its chairman said.

"It is quite certain we will not just hold on to such a good balance sheet, nor to cash holdings that will reach between four and five billion francs after the sale of Panzalim," Daniel Melin told French weekly Investir in an interview due to appear on Saturday. "We want to develop in the agro-food sector without going into consumer products..," he said.
Melin confirmed plans to sell by the end of the year to Danone a 34.5 percent stake in Panzalin, giving Danone full control over Panzalim.
He said the 2.5 to three billion francs sale would generate a "substantial" capital gain for Saint-Louis.

Melin also said that Saint-Louis already owns more than 20 percent of Spanish sugar group Azucarera and did not plan to raise that stake to more than 25 percent because it would be forced to launch a takeover bid for the company.
But if Azucarera linked up with Ebro, the top sugar group in Spain and if Saint-Louis was asked to play a role in the new entity "we would be ready to do so", Melin said.
He also said the performance of the paper sector was expected to improve as of the second half of 1996.
With destocking over, order books were filing up and prices rising.
Productivity of Arjo Wiggins Appleton in Europe is weaker in Europe than in the United States. But things are improving after heavy restructuring efforts.
"I see no reason not to achieve in that sector the same (productivity) level (in Europe) than in the United States," he said.
